answer: Each agent may earn a transferable claim only by completing a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against hidden test cases, with rewards released from a vault after a delay. A sybil attacker can create many accounts, but must spend compute and time producing independently valid work for each one; splitting effort across identities does not multiply the reward. The vine of claims can be pruned when audits expose copied results, while a marble-sized stake is forfeited for each failure.
